principles: Always show status: every mutating command emits a status block, never nothing.
Never fabricate: a checklist-derived view must be labelled distinctly and must not impersonate a milestone table.
Fail loud, not silent: display failures surface on stdout, they are not swallowed to stderr.
Honest exit codes: a display failure never fails the command, because the mutation already committed.
drivers: The CLI cannot verify the agent forwarded output, so enforcement can only guarantee the CLI always produces a block and never hides a display failure.
An existing test deliberately forbids fabricating a milestone table when no ledger exists.
The append runs after the mutation commits, so a non-zero exit would falsely imply a bad write.

options.name: checklist-derived-fallback-plus-visible-failure
pros: Always shows real per-item progress even with no milestone ledger
Distinct header preserves the anti-fabrication invariant
Render failures become visible without lying about the write
cons: Adds a new renderer and reworks the append control flow
Two header shapes to keep straight in dedup logic

options.name: reuse-milestone-status-missing-ledger-render
pros: No new renderer; milestone_status already renders a missing-ledger table
cons: Shows only a generic 'milestone ledger required' placeholder, not checklist progress
Violates the existing anti-fabrication test that forbids the Milestone Status header on no-ledger mutations

options.name: advance-freshness-gate
cons: Unsound: the CLI generates the report itself, so the gate adds friction without assurance
Cannot observe whether the user actually saw the output

rationale: Only this option satisfies both 'always show status' and 'never fabricate' while keeping honest exit semantics; reuse shows no per-item progress and breaks the anti-fabrication test, and the freshness gate is unsound because the CLI produces the very report it would gate on.

preMortem.scenario: The checklist-derived table is mistaken for a real milestone ledger
preMortem.trigger: A reader skims the header and assumes milestones are defined
preMortem.consequence: False confidence that milestone tracking exists
preMortem.mitigation: Use the explicit 'Checklist-derived ledger (no milestone ledger set)' header and assert in tests that 'Milestone Status -' is absent

preMortem.scenario: A display-render failure fails the command and callers retry the mutation
preMortem.trigger: renderChecklistDerivedLedger or a store read throws inside the append
preMortem.consequence: Double-applied mutation or spurious CI failure after a successful write
preMortem.mitigation: Catch in the append, emit a visible stdout warning, and keep exit code 0; assert the warning path in review

preMortem.scenario: Machine JSON consumers break because a table is appended
preMortem.trigger: A --json command path also renders the derived block
preMortem.mitigation: Preserve the early --json suppression and keep the --json purity regression test green

preMortem.scenario: The DONE worktree-cleanup path loses its real-ledger table
preMortem.trigger: The refactor drops the main-root fallback branch
preMortem.consequence: DONE stops showing the real Milestone Status table
preMortem.mitigation: Keep the main-root fallback in realRender and keep the existing DONE CLI append test green
